What happens when a gateway says no. Every decline a provider can return is mapped to a canonical answer: whether it is worth retrying, whether the instrument should be marked unusable, and what the customer should be told.

The built-in mapping is the default, and a business can override it at two levels — one specific gateway rule, or every rule producing one canonical code. Deleting an override restores the built-in answer rather than removing the handling.

## Endpoints

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PATCH` | [`/v1/businesses/{biz}/decline_codes/{code}`](/help/developers/api-reference/payments/override-every-rule-that-produces-one-canonical) | Override every rule that produces one canonical code |
| `DELETE` | [`/v1/businesses/{biz}/decline_codes/{code}`](/help/developers/api-reference/payments/remove-the-code-level-setting) | Remove the code-level setting |
| `GET` | [`/v1/businesses/{biz}/decline_rules`](/help/developers/api-reference/payments/list-every-gateway-decline-and-how-this-business) | List every gateway decline and how this business handles it |
| `PATCH` | [`/v1/businesses/{biz}/decline_rules/{rule}`](/help/developers/api-reference/payments/override-one-rule-s-answer-for-this-business) | Override one rule's answer for this business |
| `DELETE` | [`/v1/businesses/{biz}/decline_rules/{rule}`](/help/developers/api-reference/payments/remove-the-override-and-restore-the-built-in-ans) | Remove the override and restore the built-in answer |
